q1: Immediate priorities: (1) Airway, breathing, circulation: GCS 13, so call the ICU team for ICU-level monitoring, aspiration precautions, and readiness to protect the airway if GCS falls. Neuro checks (ICE score, GCS) every 2-4 hours. (2) ICANS, ASTCT grade 2-3 (ICE 5/10, depressed consciousness): give dexamethasone 10 mg IV every 6 hours now and escalate (e.g. methylprednisolone 1 g daily, anakinra) if he worsens. Seizure precautions; continue levetiracetam, increasing to 750-1,000 mg twice daily. (3) Concurrent CRS grade 2 (fever 38.9 C, BP 96/58): IV fluid bolus; repeat tocilizumab 8 mg/kg because the dose is not exhausted. Tocilizumab alone does not treat ICANS, and vasopressors or ICU are needed if hypotension persists. (4) Febrile neutropenia (ANC 0.2): peripheral and central-line blood cultures, then empiric broad-spectrum IV antibiotics (cefepime) within one hour. (5) Hyperglycemia: dexamethasone will worsen glucose in this diabetic patient (242 mg/dL), so start a basal-bolus insulin plan. Transfuse platelets to at least 50 before any procedure.
q2: Differential: ICANS, bacterial meningitis or HSV/HHV-6 encephalitis, intracranial hemorrhage, non-convulsive seizures, hyponatremia.
q3: Investigations: urgent non-contrast CT head to exclude hemorrhage, then MRI brain with contrast (edema, leptomeningeal enhancement, lymphoma, encephalitis). EEG to exclude non-convulsive status. Lumbar puncture only after imaging and platelet transfusion to at least 50: opening pressure, cell count, protein, glucose, Gram stain and culture, HSV and HHV-6 PCR, cytology and flow cytometry. Blood: peripheral and line blood cultures, CBC, CMP, magnesium, phosphate, CRP, ferritin, fibrinogen, INR, lactate, ammonia, glucose monitoring; urine culture and chest X-ray for the fever source.
